evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>
evidence_tree.note: The golden scenario definition (roster, champion, items, level, target resistances) is not present anywhere under data/ or docs/math-foundations.md, so the identity of sources[6] and of the Bloodsong holder could not be read directly. The computation below is therefore a ratio identification against the cached wiki text, which is exact to the displayed precision.

sources_quoted.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).
Basic attacks [[on-hit]] deal {{as|{{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}|ad}} {{as|physical damage}} to other enemies in a 350 radius ...
sources_quoted.used_for: Fixes the {{rd|A|B}} template convention: A = melee wielder, B = ranged wielder (Cleave is 40% AD melee / 20% AD ranged).

sources_quoted.quote: Reduces {{rd|30%|10%}} of all post-mitigation physical and magic damage received ...
sources_quoted.used_for: Second confirmation of the melee-first / ranged-second {{rd}} ordering.

sources_quoted.quote: Dealing physical damage to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts 6% armor reduction, up to 30% at 5 stacks. / Dealing physical damage grants you 20 bonus movement speed for 2 seconds.
sources_quoted.used_for: Rules Black Cleaver out as the source of the observed change: it carries no damage amplifier, and no admissible Carve stack transition reproduces a x1.08 damage ratio (see alternative_hypotheses).

sources_quoted.quote: Resistance mitigation (apply_resistance) | m(R)=100/(100+R); EHP round-trip raw = post*(1+R/100) ... | EXACT
sources_quoted.used_for: Mitigation is linear in the raw damage, so a pure multiplicative damage-taken amplifier scales a source's post-mitigation total by exactly the same factor, whether it is applied pre- or post-mitigation. This is what makes the ratio test exact.

step_1_observed_ratio.reading: Indistinguishable from 1.08 at the leaf's one-decimal display precision.

step_4_unamplified_base.reading: The old leaf is exactly the un-amplified source total; the new leaf is that same total with one 8% multiplicative damage-taken amplifier applied. The change is 'amplifier now applied', not 'amplifier value retuned' (a 5%->8% retune would have produced 150.29 -> 162.3, not 170.4).

step_5_attribution.amplifier: Bloodsong 'Expose Weakness' (S1): target takes 8% (melee wielder) increased damage from ALL sources for 4 s after the Spellblade-empowered attack hits a champion.
why_this_amplifier: The scenario is named 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' and Bloodsong is one of its two named items.

Bloodsong is the only item in the cached items.json whose effect is an 8%-melee 'increased damage from all sources' debuff on the target. A full sweep of every item passive/active branch matching /increased damage|amplif|vulnerab/ returned exactly one other target-side all-sources debuff, Imperial Mandate at 7% (wrong magnitude), plus self-amps of other magnitudes (Riftmaker 2%x4, Haunting Guise / Liandry's 2%x3, Immortal Path 4%, Lord Dominik's and Perplexity health-scaled).

'coupled_scenarios' + 'roster' is consistent with Expose Weakness being the one amplifier here whose wiki text explicitly reads 'from all sources', i.e. it crosses from the Bloodsong holder onto the whole roster's damage - exactly the class of leaf that a coupled-roster golden scenario exists to pin.
The debuff is applied by the Spellblade-empowered attack and lasts 4 s, so downstream sources in the same breakdown are inside its window.

independent_computation.conclusion: 170.4 is the value the cached wiki text produces: un-amplified source total 157.78 x 1.08 (Expose Weakness, melee wielder) = 170.424 -> 170.4. The old value 157.8 omitted the Expose Weakness amplifier entirely.

alternative_hypotheses_ruled_out.hypothesis: Black Cleaver Carve stack-count change moved the target's effective armor.
alternative_hypotheses_ruled_out.ruled_out_because: Carve is 6% armor reduction per stack, max 30% (S4). Requiring (100 + A*(1-r_old)) / (100 + A*(1-r_new)) = 1.08 has no solution at any realistic champion armor A for any admissible pair of Carve stack levels r in {0, .06, .12, .18, .24, .30}: e.g. A=100 with 24%->30% gives 1.0353, 0%->30% gives 1.176, and matching 1.08 exactly with the documented 0.8*max_stacks=24% model would require A=2000. A resistance-driven change would also not land on a clean 1.08.

alternative_hypotheses_ruled_out.ruled_out_as_the_named_cause_but_harmles: PtA reads 'grant you 8% increased damage against champions' - a self-amp, also exactly 8%. If the roster's amp were PtA rather than Bloodsong, the arithmetic and the verdict are unchanged (x1.08 either way). Bloodsong is the attribution named by the scenario id and is the only amp whose text says 'from all sources'.

alternative_hypotheses_ruled_out.hypothesis: both_wrong (the source should carry the amp AND something else).
alternative_hypotheses_ruled_out.ruled_out_because: Nothing in the cached data or docs/math-foundations.md prescribes a second multiplier on this source; the observed factor is exactly one Expose Weakness application, and math-foundations documents no amp-composition rule that would compound it.

residual_uncertainty.statement: The {{rd|8%|5%}} split is keyed to the Bloodsong WIELDER's range class (S2, S3): 8% melee, 5% ranged. The scenario's roster is not readable from data/ or docs/math-foundations.md, so the wielder's range class could not be confirmed from the evidence tree.
residual_uncertainty.impact: If and only if the Bloodsong wielder in 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' is a RANGED champion, the correct leaf would be 157.8 * 1.05 = 165.7 and the verdict would flip to both_wrong. The engine emitted the melee branch.
residual_uncertainty.why_the_verdict_still_stands: Black Cleaver is a melee-bruiser physical-damage item (Carve requires repeated physical damage application) and the scenario pairs it with Bloodsong on the same roster, so the melee branch is the expected reading; and in either case the direction of the change - applying Expose Weakness to this source at all - is correct per the wiki text, while the old value 157.8 (no amplifier) is wrong under every reading.
residual_uncertainty.cheapest_confirmation: Check the attack range / range class of the Bloodsong holder in the scenario roster; melee => 170.4 confirmed.
